Root read the exact extracted implementation/test selections in review chunks0/1 (evidence records, mechanical receipts, source configuration, declaration scanner and unit parser), then supplied per-source rationale and limitations. shared_typing_core independently read all23 raw unit bodies, the complete correspondence-review policy, every extracted implementation/test selection in chunks2–6, and the retained book/MathJax/CSS assets; it reconciled root findings with those selections. rationale: graph::parse tracks unique node IDs and explicit slot assignments, validates constructor/projection kinds and target existence, forbids variable-store reference targets, bounds arrays at64 and checks index bounds. A post-assignment pass uses edge_target and requires lease supports to hold owned or leased edges, so later supports work but missing/uninitialized/shared supports fail. Tests cover duplicates, unknown constructors/targets, invalid primitive/array projections, array0/64/65 boundaries, future supports and rejected targets; cycle tests confirm structural acceptance of ownership cycles. No owner exclusivity predicate is present, consistent with depicting malformed language states.
limitations: These validations are structural constraints of the diagram language, not proofs of Dada language invariants.
